authority: Fit only to primary-owner-approved anchors. Do not modify buildings, roof volumes, water, routes or terrain.

clip.note: Fits bare pipe, not the enlarged top socket. Mount tabs require a supported attachment.

outlet.note: Use an existing opening; do not cut a new drainage route.

ac_drain.note: Connect to the actual AC outlet. Particle endpoint must use the tube mouth, not the object origin.

drip_loop.note: Short accessory only. Long wire spans must follow actual approved pole/building anchors.

hinge.note: Art only; no door animation, constraint or opening authority.

catch_screen.note: Match an approved existing opening. Do not claim drainage behavior or change traversability.

cover_handle.note: Accessory on an existing cover, not a new access hole.

decal_placements: Confine damp streaks to real downpipe joints, outlet mouths and AC drip paths; keep unrelated walls dry.
Apply rust selectively at exposed roof-patch edges, fasteners and existing damaged hinge surfaces. Do not turn every maintained fitting rusty.
Keep generator soot at primary-authored exhaust anchors; these fittings do not justify new generators.
Reuse earlier poster and warning assets only on approved public-wall or fence surfaces. Do not cover utility labels or project through fittings.
vertex_painting_notes: New prop material has no vertex-color blending. Paint primary receiver meshes only through their existing material contract; do not pretend this kit supplies that shader.
Blend dust on low, exposed receiver surfaces with a soft height falloff; reduce coverage where runoff visibly washes the surface.
Concentrate algae near persistently damp, shaded receiving surfaces rather than coating exposed pipework uniformly.
For waterfront anchors, align weathering to the primary waterline and wetting exposure; do not invent a ground-level dust band over water.

scatter_clutter_prop_lists.placement: Existing service wall; use a supported landing or ground surface already supplied by primary.
Existing roof only; rotate to its slope and fit the support contact.
Existing counter and shutter; keep access clear.
Approved wall or pole anchors. No live electricity or arbitrary wiring topology.
Existing compatible drain or cover; no new opening, obstruction or collision.

micro_storytelling_vignettes.fictional_scene: A coiled hose and rinsed bucket sit beside a recently serviced tap. The wall is washed clean directly below the mouth, with older damp staining at the margins.
micro_storytelling_vignettes.constraint: Do not imply access to water is absent everywhere else.

micro_storytelling_vignettes.fictional_scene: A small replacement patch contrasts with the older sheet. A bolt strip and tool tray remain on an existing safe ledge; the repaired area is newer, not uniformly decayed.
micro_storytelling_vignettes.constraint: No new roof structure or unsupported overhead clutter.

micro_storytelling_vignettes.fictional_scene: A polished contact mark sits behind the shutter hasp. A replacement hinge and reinforced counter bracket show continued maintenance and daily use.
micro_storytelling_vignettes.constraint: Keep the shop's primary identity and opening state unchanged.

micro_storytelling_vignettes.fictional_scene: On a primary-approved Makoko household landing, a bucket and hose are kept neatly beside a repaired fitting. Wear follows splash exposure; the surrounding waterway stays open.
micro_storytelling_vignettes.constraint: Original fictional vignette, not a surveyed household. No added walkway, filled water or landmark.
